transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood DevRel), Alicia (PM), Theo (ML Eng), Marcus (SRE), Nina (Security), Ravi (Backend)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be partial): Discussed pilot stability issues around function invocation retries and KV cache miss storms. Reviewed recent benchmark artifacts. Proposed short-term mitigation (prefix caching + controlled batching) and acceptance test matrix.

00:00 Samira (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, schedule's packed so we'll try to be crisp. quick roll call?
00:08 Alicia (Bluewave PM): Alicia here, Theo, Marcus, Nina and Ravi on from my side. thanks, Samira.
00:15 Samira: great. Ethan is with me, he'll lead the latency and cache bits. Jules will note SDK changes.
00:22 Ethan (Redwood SE): hi all, quick TL;DR — we looked at the traces you sent, saw two things: function call duplication under retry and a KV cache cold-start pattern causing tail latency.
00:35 Theo (ML Eng): yeah we saw a spike—roughly at 2PM yesterday we had a burst and a bunch of requests hit the longer path. tail spiked to 1.1s on some 8k prompts which is, uh, not great.
00:45 Marcus (SRE): to add, some requests timed out in our gateway and retried which seemed to lead to duplicate tool invocation calls; that's causing downstream job contention.
00:58 Ethan: okay that maps. a couple of immediate ideas: 1) make the SDK idempotency token mandatory for function calls, 2) apply a small jittered debounce on retries client-side, and 3) adjust Redwood's prefix/KV warmup to a staged prefetch on known hot keys.
01:18 Ravi (Backend): quick Q — if we make idempotency mandatory, do we need to change our event topology? we currently pass a request-id but it's not persisted across retries.
01:29 Jules (DevRel): you'd just need to attach the idempotency token to the function call in the SDK wrapper; we can provide a tiny patch that generates or reuses request-id from headers. no topology change server-side.
01:40 Nina (Security): what's the risk surface? idempotency tokens persist across retries — are they PII? do we encrypt them? we need answers for SOC2 reviewer.
01:52 Samira: great callout. tokens are non-PII opaque GUIDs. Redwood can annotate tokens in logs but we can show redaction in audit exports. we'll include the KMS encryption details in the doc we send.
02:05 Alicia: perfect. another data point — structured output failure rate is small but enough to break our ingestion. sometimes the JSON returned has stray commas or model writes an extra field. any advice?
02:17 Ethan: two layers — first, enforce a schema on the function response using the SDK's validator; second, add a light post-parse retry that requests the model to re-conform to the schema before treating it as terminal. we've built that into our sample.
02:32 Theo: when you say validator, is that offline or enforced at runtime? curious about CPU overhead.
02:38 Jules: runtime, but very cheap — basically a JSON schema check and, if it fails, we do one corrective prompt and a re-ask. overhead is negligible compared to token generation.
02:51 Marcus: okay, but during the spike we saw a 30% drop in KV hit rate which made more calls hit the model and amplified the problem. what triggers cache eviction?
03:03 Ethan: eviction is LRU-ish plus TTL; but we saw whole-key cold starts because the cache isn't warmed after autoscale events. two mitigations: proactive warmup of expected prefixes on scale-up, and conservative TTL tuning.
03:19 Ravi: is that something we can control from our side via the SDK? like prefetch(keys)?
03:27 Ethan: yes, we'll expose a prefetch API in the SDK and also a warmup endpoint on the Redwood side you can call during your deploy hook.
03:35 Ravi: nice. please add that — we can call it in our k8s post-start hook.
03:41 Samira: note — we'll include sample k8s hook script in the repo.
03:46 Alicia: on the latency question — can we get a 95th percentile target? our SLA threshold is 350ms for interactive flows.
03:55 Ethan: candidly, for 4k tokens on hosted multi-tenant that's tough at 350ms p95. on Redwood Dedicated we can target under 350ms p95 with configuration — batching and quant profiles tuned. we'll scope benchmarks.
04:14 Theo: and for 8k tokens? we need to understand tail behavior.
04:19 Ethan: for 8k it's more variable; expect p95 in 500–800ms range on dedicated depending on batch size. with KV cache warm hits you'll see much better numbers.
04:33 Marcus: today we saw 1.1s tail — is that consistent with cold-cache + retries?
04:40 Ethan: yes, consistent. cold cache plus retry storms causes serialization on the runtime and heavier kernel paths.
04:48 Nina: circling back to security — VPC/private control plane: can we have private endpoints for the warmup API? we don't want warmup traffic over public internet.
04:59 Samira: yes for private deployments we support VPC endpoints for control plane calls; for hosted customers we offer TLS + IP allowlist and optional proxying through your VPC. we'll document options.
05:12 Alicia: awesome. another issue — duplicate tool calls — sometimes we get the same function invoked twice with identical payloads, it's creating duplicate rows.
05:23 Ethan: that aligns with the retry + no idempotency scenario. the SDK patch will include automatic dedupe by hashing the function name + payload + idempotency token.
05:37 Ravi: if we hash payloads do we leak content into logs? needs to be blind to PII.
05:43 Jules: we plan to use a keyed hash (HMAC) with customer-managed key if you prefer — that way logs are non-reversible.
05:50 Nina: that sounds more acceptable. include KMS usage in the guidance.
05:56 Samira: noted. next up — structured output stability: Theo sent a failing example in the artifact folder (link: /artifacts/bluewave/structured-fail-101.log). anyone seen it?
06:06 Theo: yeah the model inserted an extra nested object — the validator caught it, then our ingestion dropped the whole payload.
06:12 Ethan: one practical fix — have the SDK accept a "best-effort" mode where we coerce fields into the shape (e.g., flatten or drop unexpected keys) and emit a warning. that reduces breakage while you iterate.
06:24 Alicia: I'd like that as a stop-gap. long term we want schema stability — how do rollouts affect that?
06:31 Samira: Redwood rollouts can be pinned by version for a tenant; you can opt into model upgrades and run canaries. we'll include an example rollout policy that pins inference model and provides auto-fallback to last stable.
06:46 Marcus: excellent. acceptance tests — what do you recommend we run nightly to detect regressions?
06:52 Ethan: a small eval harness: 1) schema conformance suite, 2) latency regression check with synthetic 8k prompts, 3) KV hit-rate threshold check. we can provide the harness in the sample repo and run it as a GitHub action.
07:07 Ravi: please make actions easy to drop into our pipeline.
07:11 Jules: will do.
07:14 Alicia: on the pilot timeline — we want to see stability improvements in two weeks, is that feasible?
07:20 Samira: feasible if we get the logs and let Ethan run the targeted bench. that's why Ethan's item is high priority.
07:29 Theo: small nit — in our environment we observe occasional tokenization differences across model variants which affects structured output. any recommendations?
07:38 Ethan: recommend normalizing tokenization client-side where possible and pinning model family. also use Redwood's model profiling to pick the variant with consistent tokenization. we'll share the profiling link.
07:50 Nina: security checklist — we need audit logs for function calls, WORM retention options and proof of KMS key usage. can you outline what's available?
08:01 Samira: yes, Redwood audit logs include function call entries (redacted payloads optionally), and we support customer-managed keys via KMS for keys at rest. WORM retention is an add-on — we'll include the options in the SOW doc.
08:15 Nina: and SSO? we need SAML metadata and RBAC mapping for the console.
08:22 Samira: we have SAML and SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts; will send admin docs.
08:28 Alicia: quick question — can we test the warmup endpoint from our staging cluster without affecting production metrics?
08:35 Ethan: yes warmup calls are tagged and excluded from billing/metrics if you use the staging API key; we'll include the staging key pattern in the guide.
08:44 Marcus: one more SRE concern — when autoscale triggers, does Redwood pre-warm the KV on the new node or is it per-request?
08:53 Ethan: currently per-request but we will add a pre-warm hook tied to the cluster scaling event; for Dedicated we can do synchronous warmup on new instances.
09:05 Ravi: timing — can you give us patch ETA for SDK idempotency and prefetch?
09:11 Jules: ETA 3 business days for PR to the sample SDK repo; we can make it a small semver bump.
09:18 Ethan: bench run ETA 2 business days after we get the full logs.
09:22 Samira: I'll drop the pricing + SOW + security doc by Friday (2026-10-15).
09:27 Alicia: thanks. any blockers from our side? we need to get the logs and grant Ethan access to the debug bundle.
09:33 Theo: granting access now, sending bundle link in chat.
09:36 (brief pause, chat messages)
09:52 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
10:00 Ethan: quick note on batching — smaller batches reduce latency but increase cost; we recommend adaptive batching: small windows for interactive flows, larger windows for background. this is parameterizable in the SDK.
10:18 Marcus: for background jobs we can accept higher latency. interactive flows are the priority.
10:24 Alicia: ok let's codify the two profiles in the acceptance tests.
10:30 Samira: agreed. final quick recap: items and owners as we discussed; Ethan will run bench and share logs, Samira will send docs, Jules will PR SDK changes, Ravi will run staging SDK integration, Nina will collate security Qs.
10:47 Alicia: sounds good. can we meet same time next week?
10:51 Samira: same time next week works. I'll send calendar invite.
10:56 Theo: thanks everyone.
10:59 Meeting end.
